One pirate crew had a bedtime.
At eight o'clock, every light and candle went out.
Oi! I can't see my rum!
It was a rule on Bartholomew Roberts' ship.
Anyone who still wanted a drink had to take it up on the open deck.
A book from seventeen twenty-four says Roberts hoped this would curb the drinking.
One night in February seventeen twenty-two, the crew celebrated a captured ship by drinking through the liquor on board.
Next morning, a navy warship found them.
Many of the men were still drunk.
Roberts went into the fight anyway. It was his last.
